svg.title: Decision chart for the four Chapter 6 calculations

desc.style: color: rgb(34, 48, 63); fill: rgb(0, 0, 0); fill-opacity: 1; fill-rule: nonzero; stroke: none; stroke-width: 1px; stroke-opacity: 1; stroke-dasharray: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-linejoin: miter; opacity: 1; font-size: 17px; font-family: Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; text-anchor: start; dominant-baseline: auto; letter-spacing: normal; visibility: visible; paint-order: normal; marker: none;

svg.desc: Start by asking what the question wants. If it wants a speed, and gives Mach, use Airspeed Planned MACH. If it wants a speed from CAS, use Airspeed Planned TAS, which handles compressibility itself. If it wants a height for terrain clearance, that is true altitude and there is no CX-3 function — use the formula. If it wants a height for performance, that is density altitude and the CX-3 Altitude function does it.

svg.text: True altitude and density altitude both take an altitude and a temperature and give you a height.

svg.text: Ask what the answer is for: clearing the ground, or predicting the climb.

svg.text: Two sign checks that catch almost every error in this chapter

svg.text: COLD day → true altitude is LOWER than indicated. You have less clearance, not more.

text.style: color: rgb(34, 48, 63); fill: rgb(58, 48, 32); fill-opacity: 1; fill-rule: nonzero; stroke: none; stroke-width: 1px; stroke-opacity: 1; stroke-dasharray: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-linejoin: miter; opacity: 1; font-size: 13px; font-family: Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; text-anchor: middle; dominant-baseline: auto; letter-spacing: normal; visibility: visible; paint-order: normal; marker: none;

svg.text: HOT day → density altitude is HIGHER than pressure altitude. You have less performance.

text.style: color: rgb(34, 48, 63); fill: rgb(122, 106, 72); fill-opacity: 1; fill-rule: nonzero; stroke: none; stroke-width: 1px; stroke-opacity: 1; stroke-dasharray: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-linejoin: miter; opacity: 1; font-size: 12px; font-family: Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-style: italic; text-anchor: middle; dominant-baseline: auto; letter-spacing: normal; visibility: visible; paint-order: normal; marker: none;

svg.text: Both bad conditions push the number the way that costs you something. That is how you remember them.
